implementation_notes: Rust has no view engine in the standard library, so the helper is whatever the chosen engine can call: Tera exposes register_filter, register_function and register_test on the engine, and a helper is an ordinary Rust function that receives the piped value plus the call arguments and returns the engine's result type. Types replace the helper class - the render context is a serializable view model, and everything the helper needs arrives as an argument (keyword arguments included) instead of being reached through global state, and result values are built through the engine's string constructors so the escaping decision (escaped vs explicitly safe) is visible in the helper. Keep the context a presentation shape (formatted strings or primitives), not the domain entities, so helpers stay pure value transformers. A context struct with helper methods is the justified classic form when several templates share derived fields (a precomputed view model) rather than accumulating registered filters.
pitfalls: A filter that returns Err aborts the whole render; decide deliberately between failing the page and returning a fallback - unwrap_or_default is a silent fallback, not a policy.
Value::safe_string() disables escaping for the produced fragment while Value::normal_string() keeps it on; reach for the safe constructor only for markup you built yourself.
Kwargs::get converts at run time, so a template passing the wrong argument type fails while rendering; there is no compile-time check that the template supplies what the filter expects.
One Tera instance is one helper namespace, so tests that mutate a shared engine leak filters into each other; build the engine per test.

variants.name: askama derive templates with a typed context (compile time)
variants.idiom_name: #[derive(Template)] context struct with helper methods (compile-time helpers)
variants.implementation_notes: With askama the template is compiled into the binary: the derive links it to a struct or enum that defines the context, implements Template (and Display) for it, and resolves every name the template uses at compile time. A helper is therefore a plain Rust item - a method on the context struct or a function the context exposes - and nothing is looked up by name while rendering, so a missing or renamed helper is a build error and rendering allocates only the output. Choose this variant where templates can be part of the build and type safety is worth more than runtime-editable templates; askama also provides a filters module for the standard formatting filters.
pitfalls: Every name the template mentions must exist at compile time - protective during refactoring, but it means no hot-reloading of templates and a template typo becomes a build failure.
The context struct is the template's contract: keep it a purpose-built view model rather than a projection of a domain entity, or every domain change ripples into the templates.
Autoescaping depends on the template's content type hint; an inline source string without ext = "html" loses HTML escaping.
